Translate JusPrin into upstream OrcaSlicer's 22 languages

JusPrin's own windows and its AI and Home pages showed English in every
language. Every string a person reads in them is now marked and translated
into the 22 languages upstream ships, in catalogs of the fork's own so that
taking an upstream release never conflicts in one:

- Localization/native/<lang>.po for native text, collected by
  Localization/update_catalogs.py (text upstream's template already has
  keeps upstream's translation) and merged by Brand/brand_catalogs.py into
  the catalog the app loads.
- Localization/pages/<lang>.po for both pages, through Lingui 5.9.5. The app
  passes its language as ?lang=; the page activates it before any module
  runs.

Text the model reads (prompts, skills, tool results), logs, error reports,
identifiers and names stay English. The translations are machine-made and
marked "# AI Translated"; entries a translator was unsure of also carry
"# Needs human review: <what to check>". Terms follow upstream's catalog
and the OrcaSlicer localization glossary.

Sentences that were built from translated pieces are now one message each,
with placeholders and plural forms, and render the same English. Other
changes the translation needed:

- Support/Translate.hpp: GUI-free code marks text with L() and translates it
  with translated() and translated_plural(), which the app installs.
- "Model" and "Search models" in the printer picker, and "Plate" in the
  add-printer form, have contexts of their own, apart from the AI model and
  the project plate.
- Numbers JusPrin shows use the app language's separators
  (Support/DecimalText on the native side, decimalText on the pages): a
  German app reads "Kobra 3 · 0,4 mm".
